destopy.changes: python_utils/astro_function_jit.py, see destopy-code.diff: (1) SPICE kernels loaded once per process instead of kclear+furnsh in every derivative call; (2) the r mode interpolants and the mean interpolant evaluated as one stacked RegularGridInterpolator call; (3) UKF: one pool of 2 worker processes for the whole run (original: a new pool of cpu_count()-1 = 27 processes every step), per-step checkpoint/resume. Checked bit-identical: derivative (12 random states) and a full 1-hour sigma-point propagation equal to the original code (max abs diff 0). (4) BUG FIX (changes results only where the bug fires): DESTO (MATLAB) propagates all sigma points in one call and wraps every sigma point's true longitude L to [0, 2pi] when the NOMINAL sigma point's L is outside [-pi/2, pi/2]; DESTOPy propagates one sigma point per call, so the rule was evaluated per point and, when an object's L was near -pi/2 at an update epoch, the sigma points were split by 2pi. The unpatched first attempt diverged this way at step 7 (object 1807, L = -1.5707 rad; L sigma jumped to 42 rad, then SVD failure at step 9). The fix re-applies the rule with the nominal point's decision after pool.map and leaves points whose own decision matched untouched.
caveats: Pseudo-observations: DESTOPy builds the hourly orbit measurement at time t from the 'nearest newer' element set, comparing python-sgp4's jdsatepoch (the day-start part of the epoch) with t, so it normally uses an element set from a later UTC day (epoch up to ~2 days after t). The filtered estimate at t therefore carries element-set information from after t; it is causal only with respect to the measurement sequence. On 2026-04-28 (end of the allowed epoch range) DESTOPy falls back to the last element set found (first one of 04-28).
BC priors have a 1% initial sigma and 1e-16 process noise (notebook defaults), so the density scale is tied to DESTOPy's BCdata.txt values.
The ROM covers 100-800 km and the training period 1999-2010 of JB2008.
